Leather.title: Ethiopian leather
Leather.lead: International buyers already recognize distinct Ethiopian hide and skin types — for shoe uppers, fashion suede, gloves, and refined small goods — not only for livestock volume.
Leather.materialsLead: Trade has long named Ethiopian cattle, goat, and sheep materials by type. Each serves different product lines.
Leather.materialsSource: Livestock figures and potential supply based on CSA 2020/2021 survey reporting. Grade names reflect common international trade usage.
Leather.cattleBody: Known for a fine grain pattern and compact fiber structure from highland and regional herds.
Leather.cattleUse: Often chosen for quality shoe uppers, belts, and structured leather goods.
Leather.goatBody: Highland “Bati-genuine” and lowland “Bati-type” skins are valued for thickness, flexibility, and a clean inner surface.
Leather.goatUse: In demand for fashion suede, garments, and soft footwear components.
Leather.sheepBody: Compact, clean highland hair sheep skins — often called Selale type — are prized for dress glove, garment, and fine leather uses.
Leather.sheepUse: A preferred raw material for gloves, cabretta, and light yet durable accessories.
Leather.sheepLead: Sheep living in Ethiopia’s highlands produce a hair-sheep skin with dense fiber — light and soft in the hand, yet strong enough for precise cutting and finishing.
Leather.sheepPoint1: Can be worked very thin — around 0.35 mm — while keeping tensile strength for gloves and fine goods
Leather.sheepPoint2: Dense fiber and tight grain support dress gloves, sport gloves, garments, and refined small leather goods
Leather.sheepPoint3: Finished by Ethiopian tanners with a wide range of colors and surface expressions
Leather.sheepClose: This is why highland sheep leather keeps drawing international attention beyond ordinary commodity stock.
Leather.usesLead: The same livestock base supports very different product paths — from technical glove leather to everyday accessories.
Leather.useGlovesBody: Thin, strong highland sheep leather for dress and sport gloves.
Leather.useSuedeBody: Bati goat skins for soft, flexible garment and footwear surfaces.
Leather.useUppersBody: Zebu-type cattle hide for fine grain and structured footwear.
Leather.useGoodsBody: Workshop-finished pieces where hand detail and highland material meet.
Leather.exportLead: Trade routes differ by product stage. Prepared sheep leather often moves to Asian manufacturing hubs, while finished articles and footwear more often reach buyers in the United States and Europe.
Leather.exportArticlesNote: Bags, small goods and related articles, 2024
Leather.exportSource: Sources: WITS / UN Comtrade (HS sheep leather, 2023); OEC leather articles (2024); leather footwear trade aggregates (2024). Values rounded. Bars are scaled within each chart.
Leather.chainBody: Addis Hands focuses further along the chain — highland-sourced material shaped in Ethiopian workshops — so buyers can compare makers, materials, and commercial details in one place.
Leather.exploreBody: Browse curated Ethiopian companies and products — including flexible conversations on MOQ — ready for buyer inquiry.

About.title: About Addis Hands
About.lead: Addis Hands is a curated B2B showcase connecting Ethiopian leather and craft SMEs with buyers who need trustworthy export partners.
About.storyBody: We gather maker profiles, product lines, and practical trading details — photos, materials, MOQ, lead time — in one place. Buyers can browse with confidence and inquire directly when a workshop looks like a fit.
About.whyBody: Working closely with Ethiopian leather workshops, we kept seeing the same gap: strong craftsmanship, weak routes to overseas buyers. Addis Hands exists to keep that connection practical and ongoing — not as an open free-for-all marketplace, but as a carefully presented bridge.
About.curatedBody: Every company is curated. We look for makers who can show real production capacity, clear commercial terms, and product stories buyers can evaluate without guesswork.
About.whoProject: KOICA Project for Enhancing Competitiveness of the Leather and Leather Products Industry in Ethiopia
About.whoBody: Addis Hands is operated under this KOICA project. Our project team works with Ethiopian workshops to keep buyer–maker connections practical and ongoing.
About.ctaLead: Tell us who you are — we will follow up personally.
